intro: Exam-style performance-based tasks for A+ Core 2: Windows tools and commands, permissions, social engineering, change management and Linux basics.

questions.title: Windows command line
questions.scenario: A user's PC is acting up. Recall the command for each diagnostic or repair task.

activities.title: Type the command
activities.prompt: Enter the command with its switch (case does not matter).

rows.label: Scan and repair protected system files
Renew the DHCP lease
Force an immediate group policy refresh
List running processes
Check a disk for errors and fix them
Show the full IP configuration including the MAC address

questions.explanation: sfc /scannow repairs protected files, ipconfig /renew gets a new lease, gpupdate /force refreshes policy, tasklist lists processes, chkdsk /f (or /r) repairs the file system and ipconfig /all shows full configuration including the MAC address.

questions.title: Windows tools
questions.scenario: Pick the Windows tool for each job.

activities.title: Match the job to the tool
activities.prompt: Drag each job to the tool you would open.

items.text: End a frozen app and see CPU usage
Roll back a bad driver
Initialize a new disk and create a volume
Read the error logged when a service failed to start
Set a service's startup type to Disabled
Enforce a password policy on a Pro machine

activities.title: Name the console
activities.prompt: Type the run command (for example taskmgr).

rows.label: Device Manager
Services
Disk Management
Event Viewer

questions.explanation: Task Manager manages processes, Device Manager manages drivers, Disk Management handles volumes, Event Viewer shows logs, Services sets startup types and Group Policy Editor (gpedit.msc) applies policy on Pro editions.

questions.title: Share and NTFS permissions
questions.scenario: A folder is shared on the network. Work out the effective permission a user gets over the network, which is the more restrictive of the share and NTFS permissions.

activities.title: Effective permission over the network
activities.prompt: Enter Read, Change or Full Control.

rows.label: Share: Full Control, NTFS: Read
Share: Read, NTFS: Modify
Share: Change, NTFS: Full Control
Share: Full Control, NTFS: Full Control

activities.title: Match the term to its meaning
activities.prompt: Drag each statement to the term.

items.text: Child folders receive the parent's permissions
Overrides any allow for the same user or group
The object takes the destination folder's permissions
The object keeps its original permissions

questions.explanation: Over the network, the most restrictive of share and NTFS permissions applies. NTFS permissions are inherited; an explicit deny wins. Moving a file within a volume keeps its permissions, while copying or moving to another volume takes the destination's.

questions.title: Recognize the attack
questions.scenario: Security awareness training starts today. Match each scenario to the attack it describes.

activities.title: Match scenario to attack
activities.prompt: Drag each scenario to the attack.

items.text: An email link leads to a fake sign-in page
A caller claims to be the bank's fraud team
Someone watches you type a PIN
A stranger follows an employee through a badge door
Digging through trash for printed account numbers
A Wi-Fi network named like the cafe's, run by an attacker

activities.title: Defences
activities.prompt: Name one control that mitigates each (one or two words).

rows.label: Stops tailgating at a door (a small vestibule with two doors)
Stops useful data being recovered from paper (destroy it)
Second login step that defeats a stolen password

questions.explanation: Phishing is email, vishing is voice, shoulder surfing is observation, tailgating follows someone through a door, dumpster diving digs through trash, and an evil twin impersonates a trusted access point. Mantraps stop tailgating, shredders handle paper, and MFA limits the damage of stolen passwords.

questions.title: Change management and backups
questions.scenario: You are preparing to patch a production server. Put the change process in order, then match each backup type to its description.

activities.title: Order the change management process
items: Define the purpose and scope of the change
Write the plan, including a backout plan
Get approval from the change board
Document the change and its results

activities.title: Match the backup type
activities.prompt: Drag each description to the backup type.

items.text: Copies everything and clears the archive bit
Copies only what changed since the last backup of any kind
Copies everything changed since the last full backup
Fastest to back up but slowest restore (many pieces)
Restore needs only the full and the latest of these

questions.explanation: A change moves from request and risk analysis through planning with a rollback plan, approval, implementation and documentation. Incremental backups are quick but restores need the last full plus every increment; differential backups grow each day but restores need only the full plus the latest differential.

questions.title: Linux and macOS commands
questions.scenario: Many IT shops mix Windows with Linux and macOS. Match each command to its purpose.

activities.title: Match command to purpose
activities.prompt: Drag each command to what it does.

items.text: ls
chmod
pwd
grep
ps
chown

rows.label: Run a single command with elevated privileges
Show disk space by file system
Copy files and directories
Download and install packages on Ubuntu or Debian

questions.explanation: ls lists, chmod changes permissions, pwd prints the working directory, grep searches text, ps lists processes and chown changes ownership. sudo elevates, df shows free space, cp copies and apt installs packages on Debian-based systems.
